fix.note: Everyday speech often uses 머리 for 'head/brains'.

ex.en: Your brain gets tired when you don't sleep.
Exercise is good for brain health too.
What foods are good for the brain?
The teacher pointed out my pronunciation.
Thanks for pointing out my mistake.
My team leader points out every little thing.
Did you go vote yesterday?
We vote to decide the lunch menu.
I voted for my friend for class president.
It's so cold out that my ears are freezing.
The puppy's ears are really big.
My ears hurt from listening to loud music.

fix.note: ㄹ drops before ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ: 느는, 늡니다. Transitive: 늘리다.

ex.en: My Korean improved a lot from practicing every day.
I'm busy these days because work has increased.
The café has gotten a lot more customers.
We eat traditional food on Lunar New Year.

ex.s: 이 시장은 백 년의 전통이 있어요.
ex.en: This market has a hundred years of tradition.
Our family values tradition.
I'm in my early thirties.
The beginning of the movie was a bit boring.
We scored a goal early in the game.

notes: Honorific agreement (선생님/팀장님 지적), wrong conjugation in 늘다 note (는→느는), awkward collocations (전통이 오래됐어요, 다음 달 초반), translation fixes; dropped 보고 as duplicate of 보고하다.
